title: Warp shows how human feedback can improve agents over time
friendlyTitle: Warp teaches AI agents to learn from human feedback
summary: Warp describes a two-skill pattern in which a task agent uses a domain-specific skill while a scheduled improver reviews accumulated human feedback and proposes small edits to that skill. The changes remain visible and can pass through normal pull-request review before affecting future runs.
friendlySummary: One AI agent does the work, while another checks human feedback and suggests small updates to its instructions. People review the updates before they are used.
whyItMatters: Teams can make recurring agents better without relying on opaque retraining or ever-larger prompts. Keeping improvements as reviewable files also gives people a practical control point for quality and governance.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This can help a work assistant improve safely over time instead of making the same mistake again.
